questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of clot retention after TURP.

questions.stem: True urine output = total drained minus irrigation infused. Using the 1600 and 1700 rows, what was the client's true urine output over those 2 hours? Record your answer in mL.

rationale.correct: (1,250 + 1,100) - (1,000 + 1,000) = 2,350 - 2,000 = 350 mL over 2 hours. At 1800, drainage (650) is less than the irrigation (1,000), so 350 mL of irrigant is retained in the bladder.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Which parts of the plan should the nurse include for CBI? Select all that apply.

options.text: Adjust the irrigation rate to keep drainage light pink
Record irrigation in and drainage out to calculate true urine output
Keep traction on the catheter as prescribed
Encourage the client to try to void around the catheter
Let the irrigation bag run dry between changes

rationale.correct: Titrate irrigation to color, track true output, maintain traction and use isotonic fluid.

perOption.c: Compresses the prostate bed to reduce bleeding.
perOption.d: Hypotonic fluid can cause hemolysis and hyponatremia.

questions.stem: At 2300, the client is confused and nauseated. Review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Prepare hypertonic saline or a loop diuretic as prescribed

questions.stem: Before discharge, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "Some blood in the urine for a few weeks can be normal, but I'll call if it gets thick or has clots."
"I'll avoid straining, heavy lifting and driving for a few weeks."

questions.educationalObjective: Generate a plan for graft dysfunction.

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: Admit. Biopsy tomorrow. Hold tacrolimus today. Stop clarithromycin.

questions.stem: The biopsy shows acute cellular rejection; IV methylprednisolone pulses are started. Which actions should the nurse take to keep the client safe? Select all that apply.

options.text: Draw tacrolimus troughs just before the morning dose
Give tacrolimus at the same times daily, the same way with food
Record the clarithromycin interaction in the chart
Teach the client to tell every prescriber about the transplant
Draw the tacrolimus level 2 hours after the morning dose
Allow grapefruit juice with breakfast if the client prefers it

rationale.correct: Correct trough timing, consistent dosing and interaction alerts keep immunosuppression safe.

perOption.e: That is a peak, not a trough.

caseStudies.title: TURP with bladder irrigation and TUR syndrome

exhibits.title: Urology unit, 2 hours after surgery
exhibits.body: A 72-year-old client had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) this afternoon. A three-way catheter with continuous bladder irrigation (CBI) is in place, with 0.9% sodium chloride irrigation.

rows.label: Client report
cells: Severe lower abdominal pain, urge to void

rows.label: Bladder
cells: Firm and distended above the pubis

caseStudies.title: Kidney transplant rejection and tacrolimus toxicity

exhibits.title: Transplant clinic
exhibits.body: A 42-year-old client had a deceased-donor kidney transplant 4 months ago and takes tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone. The client started clarithromycin from an urgent care clinic 5 days ago and missed 2 days of mycophenolate last week because of nausea. Today the client has tenderness over the transplanted kidney, less urine and a tremor.

caseStudies.title: Anemia and mineral bone disease of chronic kidney disease

exhibits.title: Nephrology clinic
exhibits.body: A 64-year-old client with stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 22) is tired and short of breath on stairs. The client has itchy skin and leg cramps. Medicines: lisinopril, furosemide, calcium carbonate with meals.

exhibits.title: Hemodialysis unit, first treatment
exhibits.body: A 59-year-old client with kidney failure (BUN 168 mg/dL) begins hemodialysis today through a new left upper arm arteriovenous fistula created 3 months ago. In the last hour of a 3-hour run, the client reports a headache and nausea and becomes restless and confused.
